drivers.label: Proxmox LXC
drivers.description: Linux boxes, with or without a desktop, as containers on a Proxmox VE host.

fields.label: API URL
fields.description: For example https://192.0.2.10:8006/api2/json, as the setup guide's token file gives it.

fields.label: Node
fields.description: The node boxes run on. Leave empty on a single-node host.

fields.label: TLS fingerprint
fields.description: The SHA-256 fingerprint of the Proxmox API's certificate, from the setup guide's token file. bb-box then trusts that certificate alone. Leave empty to check the certificate against its CA.

fields.label: CA certificate
fields.description: PEM certificate of the CA that signed the Proxmox API's certificate, when there is no TLS fingerprint. Leave empty for a publicly trusted one.

fields.label: API token ID
fields.description: For example bbbox@pve!plugin. The setup guide lists the privileges it needs.

fields.label: API token secret
fields.description: The secret of the API token, from the setup guide's token file.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.description: The unencrypted OpenSSH private key the templates were built with (the setup guide's BBBOX_SSH_KEY). Leave empty and bb-box makes one and shows its public key, which the templates must then accept.

fields.label: Resource pool
fields.description: Boxes are made in this pool. The token needs rights on it.

fields.label: Linux templates
fields.description: VMIDs of the CT templates linux boxes are linked clones of, separated by spaces or commas. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: GPU desktop templates
fields.description: One line per GPU desktop template that linux-desktop boxes are linked clones of: its VMID, a space and the ID of the GPU it carries, such as the UUID nvidia-smi -L shows. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: CPU desktop templates
fields.description: VMIDs of the CPU-only desktop templates linux-desktop-cpu boxes are linked clones of, separated by spaces or commas. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: CPU Wayland desktop templates
fields.description: VMIDs of the CPU-only Wayland desktop templates linux-desktop-wayland-cpu boxes are linked clones of, separated by spaces or commas. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Desktops per GPU
fields.description: A new linux-desktop box goes to the GPU with the fewest desktops, and is refused when every GPU runs this many. 0 means no limit.

fields.label: Network bridge
fields.description: The bridge boxes attach to.

fields.label: Subnet
fields.description: The bridge's subnet in CIDR form. Boxes get static addresses; there is no DHCP.

fields.label: Gateway
fields.description: The host's address on the bridge.

fields.label: Box addresses
fields.description: The range bb-box hands out. The n-th VMID gets the n-th address. Leave empty to use the whole subnet except the gateway.

fields.label: First box VMID
fields.description: Boxes take VMIDs from this range. Keep other guests out of it.

fields.label: Last box VMID
fields.description: The end of the range boxes take VMIDs from.

fields.label: SSH user
fields.description: The user in the templates that bb-box and BB work as.

fields.label: Memory kept free (MiB)
fields.description: A new box is refused if the node would have less memory than this left.

fields.label: Disk kept free (GiB)
fields.description: A new box is refused if the template's storage has less free space than this.

drivers.label: Proxmox QEMU
drivers.description: Windows desktops as VMs on a Proxmox VE host.

fields.label: API URL
fields.description: For example https://192.0.2.10:8006/api2/json, as the Proxmox LXC setup guide's token file gives it. Leave it, the token, the fingerprint and the CA certificate empty to use Proxmox LXC's.

fields.label: Node
fields.description: The node boxes run on. Leave empty on a single-node host.

fields.label: TLS fingerprint
fields.description: The SHA-256 fingerprint of the Proxmox API's certificate, from the setup guide's token file. bb-box then trusts that certificate alone. Leave empty to check the certificate against its CA.

fields.label: CA certificate
fields.description: PEM certificate of the CA that signed the Proxmox API's certificate, when there is no TLS fingerprint. Leave empty for a publicly trusted one.

fields.label: API token ID
fields.description: For example bbbox@pve!plugin. The setup guide lists the privileges it needs.

fields.label: API token secret
fields.description: The secret of the API token, from the setup guide's token file.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.description: Paste BBBOX_SSH_KEY, the private key build.sh put in the template, or leave it empty to use Proxmox LXC's. With neither, bb-box makes a key, which the template does not accept until you add its public key.

fields.label: Resource pool
fields.description: Boxes are made in this pool. The token needs rights on it.

fields.label: Windows templates
fields.description: VMIDs of the Windows templates windows-desktop boxes are linked clones of, separated by spaces or commas. setup/proxmox-qemu/build.sh builds one. A new box is cloned from the least used.

fields.label: Linux templates
fields.description: VMIDs of the Linux templates that linux boxes as VMs are linked clones of, separated by spaces or commas, for a box with its own kernel. setup/proxmox-qemu/build.sh linux builds one. Empty offers no Linux VMs.

fields.label: Linux desktop templates
fields.description: VMIDs of the Linux desktop templates that linux-desktop-cpu boxes as VMs are linked clones of, separated by spaces or commas, for a desktop with its own kernel. setup/proxmox-qemu/build.sh linux-desktop builds one. Empty offers no Linux desktop VMs.

fields.label: Android templates
fields.description: VMIDs of the Android templates, separated by spaces or commas: the Linux template with the Android SDK, the emulator and a booted device for each model. setup/proxmox-qemu/build.sh android builds one, on a host with nested virtualization, and the nightly job refreshes it monthly. bb-box offers android boxes from it while linux-kvm is on and its record lists its devices.

fields.label: Windows boxes as BB machines
fields.description: Windows boxes join BB as machines, so threads and terminals can use them, as Linux and macOS boxes do. Off, they are boxes only.

fields.label: KVM in Linux VM boxes
fields.description: Linux VM boxes can run VMs of their own through /dev/kvm, and linux-kvm asks for one. Turn it on when the host allows nested virtualization: build.sh linux says whether /dev/kvm works in a clone.

fields.label: Network bridge
fields.description: The bridge boxes attach to.

fields.label: Subnet
fields.description: The bridge's subnet in CIDR form. Boxes get static addresses; there is no DHCP.

fields.label: Gateway
fields.description: The host's address on the bridge.

fields.label: Box addresses
fields.description: The range bb-box hands out. The n-th VMID gets the n-th address. Keep it apart from the Proxmox LXC backend's. Leave empty to use the whole subnet except the gateway.

fields.label: First box VMID
fields.description: Boxes take VMIDs from this range. Keep other guests out of it, the Proxmox LXC backend's too.

fields.label: Last box VMID
fields.description: The end of the range boxes take VMIDs from.

fields.label: SSH user
fields.description: The user in the template that bb-box and BB work as.

fields.label: Memory kept free (MiB)
fields.description: A new box is refused if the node would have less memory than this left.

fields.label: Disk kept free (GiB)
fields.description: A new box is refused if the template's storage has less free space than this.

drivers.label: SSH host pool
drivers.description: Your own Linux machines and Macs, reached over SSH and reset between boxes.

fields.label: Machines
fields.description: One line per machine: a name, [user@]host[:port], its kinds, and optionally via=<jump host>, reset=machine and labels=<words>. For example "build-1 192.0.2.21 linux" or "mac-mini 192.0.2.30 macos,macos-desktop". ios on a Mac lends iOS slots there, each a macOS user with its own device, for ios boxes asked for with shared: true; ios:<slots> sets how many, where bb-box would estimate them from the Mac. setup/ssh-pool/setup.sh, or setup-mac.sh on a Mac, prints the line for each machine.

fields.label: Host keys
fields.description: known_hosts lines for every machine and jump host, as setup.sh and setup-mac.sh print them. bb-box connects only to a machine whose key is here.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.description: An unencrypted OpenSSH private key that the machines' admin user accepts. Leave empty and bb-box makes one and shows its public key, which you then give setup.sh.

fields.label: Slots for ios boxes per Mac
fields.description: The most iOS slots a Mac whose line lists ios has making, ready or held at once. It is lent whole only while it lends none. Unset, bb-box estimates it for each Mac: the fewest of its cores over 1.3, its memory over 1.5 GiB after 8 GiB for the Mac, and what its video encoder allows. ios:<slots> on a Mac's line wins.

fields.label: Ready slots for ios boxes kept on a Mac
fields.description: Slots a Mac whose line lists ios keeps ready while it is not lent whole, so the next ios box is ready in seconds.

fields.label: Slots a Mac sweeps at once
fields.description: The most released iOS slots whose files a Mac sweeps in one pass.

fields.label: Disk a Mac keeps free of slots (GiB)
fields.description: A Mac makes no new iOS slot while it has less free disk than this.

drivers.label: Tart
drivers.description: macOS boxes, iOS Simulator boxes, and Linux and Windows boxes on arm64, as VMs on your Macs with Apple silicon.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.description: The unencrypted OpenSSH private key that each Mac's user and each image's VM user accept. Leave empty and bb-box makes one and shows its public key.

fields.label: macOS image
fields.description: The Tart VM on each Mac that macos boxes, with no desktop shown, are cloned from. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: macOS desktop image
fields.description: The Tart VM on each Mac that macos-desktop boxes are cloned from. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Linux image (arm64)
fields.description: The Tart VM on each Mac that linux-arm64 boxes are cloned from, as setup/tart/prepare-linux-image.sh builds it (bb-box-linux). Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Linux desktop image (arm64)
fields.description: The Tart VM on each Mac that linux-arm64-desktop-cpu boxes are cloned from, as setup/tart/prepare-linux-image.sh --desktop builds it (bb-box-linux-desktop). Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Windows image (arm64)
fields.description: The Windows image on each Mac, in ~/.bb-box/qemu/images, that windows-arm64-desktop boxes are made from, run by QEMU. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: iOS image
fields.description: The Tart VM on each Mac that ios boxes are cloned from, as setup/tart/prepare-ios-image.sh builds it on the macOS image (bb-box-ios): idb_companion and a booted-once, slimmed iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 17 and iPad Pro 13-inch (M5). bb-box checks and refreshes it with the macOS image. Empty, the default, turns it off. ios boxes are not offered yet.

fields.label: Shared iOS hosts
fields.description: ios boxes asked for with shared: true take a slot, a macOS user with its own device, on a VM of the iOS image made as a shared host: made when a box needs one, deleted when its last box is released. Off by default.

fields.label: Windows boxes as BB machines
fields.description: Windows boxes join BB as machines, so threads and terminals can use them, as Linux and macOS boxes do. Off, they are boxes only.

fields.label: Video by default for macOS desktops
fields.description: macOS desktops open as video, from bb-box-stream in the image, not VNC. Off by default: they open as VNC, which is already smooth on a Tart Mac, at 52 to 55 frames a second, and a person can choose video under Display. Video uses much less bandwidth, about 1.2 Mbit/s against 20 while scrolling, but a key shows a little later, about 57 ms against 31.

fields.label: VM user
fields.description: The user in the macOS images that bb-box and BB work as. It is logged in to the desktop automatically. Linux boxes work as box.

fields.label: VMs per Mac
fields.description: The most macOS VMs that run on each Mac at once, counting every VM Tart runs there, not only bb-box's. At most 2, which Apple's licence and the Virtualization framework allow.

fields.label: Memory kept free (MiB)
fields.description: A new box is refused if the Mac would have less memory than this left for its own use, after its running VMs.

fields.label: Disk kept free (GiB)
fields.description: A new box is refused if the Mac's disk has less free space than this.

fields.label: Hours a macOS warm VM or spare is kept
fields.description: A suspended macOS warm VM, or a spare that waits suspended, saved longer ago than this is replaced by a fresh one, as an old saved state may not restore.

fields.label: Slots per shared iOS host
fields.description: The most slots a shared iOS host has making, ready or held at once. Unset, bb-box estimates it for each Mac: the fewest of the host's cores over 1.3, its memory over 1.5 GiB after 8 GiB for the host, and what the Mac's video encoder allows. A Mac's own value wins.

fields.label: Ready slots kept on a shared iOS host
fields.description: Slots a shared iOS host keeps ready while it holds a box, so the next box is ready in seconds.

fields.label: Slots a shared iOS host sweeps at once
fields.description: The most released slots whose files a shared iOS host sweeps in one pass.

fields.label: Cores of a shared iOS host
fields.description: The cores of each shared iOS host's VM, shared by its slots. Unset, the Mac's performance cores. A Mac's own value wins.

fields.label: Memory of a shared iOS host (GiB)
fields.description: The memory of each shared iOS host's VM, shared by its slots. Unset, 8 GiB for the host and 1.5 GiB for each slot, within the Mac's memory. A Mac's own value wins.

fields.label: Shared iOS hosts per Mac
fields.description: The most shared iOS hosts a Mac runs. Each is one of the Mac's two macOS VMs, and both share the Mac's video encoder.

fields.label: Disk a shared iOS host keeps free (GiB)
fields.description: A shared iOS host makes no new slot while its VM has less free disk than this.

hostFields.label: Address
hostFields.description: The Mac's address, with :port when SSH is not on 22. For example 192.0.2.20.

hostFields.label: User
hostFields.description: The user bb-box logs in to the Mac as, which runs tart.

hostFields.label: Host keys
hostFields.description: The Mac's SSH host keys as known_hosts lines. ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 <address> prints one. bb-box checks them on every connection.

hostFields.label: Slots per shared iOS host
hostFields.description: The most slots a shared iOS host on this Mac has, over the backend's setting and bb-box's estimate for the Mac. Empty for those.

hostFields.label: Cores of a shared iOS host
hostFields.description: The cores of a shared iOS host's VM on this Mac, over the backend's setting and the Mac's performance cores. Empty for those.

hostFields.label: Memory of a shared iOS host (GiB)
hostFields.description: The memory of a shared iOS host's VM on this Mac, over the backend's setting and bb-box's estimate. Empty for those.

drivers.label: Docker
drivers.description: Linux boxes, with or without a desktop, as containers on a Docker host. It needs only Docker.

fields.label: Host
fields.description: Where the Docker daemon is, as unix:///path/to/docker.sock, ssh://user@host, or bb:<machine ID> for a BB machine, which bb-box reaches through BB. Empty uses the docker CLI's own default on BB's server: DOCKER_HOST, its current context, or the local socket. Over SSH, BB's server user must log in without a prompt.

fields.label: Linux image
fields.description: The image linux boxes run. setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Desktop image
fields.description: The image linux-desktop-cpu boxes, and linux-desktop boxes when GPU desktops are on, run. setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Wayland desktop image
fields.description: The image linux-desktop-wayland-cpu boxes run: Sway on Wayland, drawn by the CPU. setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Docker in boxes
fields.description: Give each box its own Docker daemon, started by its first docker command. Each runs as a privileged container, which can take over the Docker host. Off, or on rootless Docker, boxes say No Docker.

fields.label: GPU desktops
fields.description: Offer linux-desktop boxes on the host's NVIDIA GPUs, which the NVIDIA Container Toolkit lists as CDI devices (nvidia-ctk cdi generate).

fields.label: Desktops per GPU
fields.description: The most linux-desktop boxes that share one GPU.

fields.label: Network
fields.description: The Docker network bb-box makes for its boxes, apart from the host's other containers.

fields.label: Most boxes
fields.description: The most bb-box containers on the host at once, running or stopped, counting those of every bb-box install that uses it.

fields.label: Memory kept free (MiB)
fields.description: A new box is refused if the host would have less memory than this left, after the memory limits of the running boxes.

drivers.label: microsandbox
drivers.description: Linux boxes, with or without a desktop, as microVMs that start in under a second, on a Linux host with KVM or a Mac. bb-box installs its own msb there.

fields.label: Host
fields.description: The host that runs the boxes, a Linux host with KVM or a Mac: ssh://user@host, or bb:<machine ID> for a BB machine, which bb-box reaches through BB. Empty uses BB's server. bb-box installs its own msb there, in a folder of its own.

fields.label: Linux image
fields.description: The image linux boxes run. bb-box imports it from Docker on the host, where setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Desktop image
fields.description: The image linux-desktop-cpu boxes run. bb-box imports it from Docker on the host, where setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Linux image (arm64)
fields.description: The image linux-arm64 boxes run, on an arm64 host such as a Mac. bb-box imports it from Docker on the host, or builds it there with setup/docker/build.sh --arch arm64 in a microVM of its own. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Desktop image (arm64)
fields.description: The image linux-arm64-desktop-cpu boxes run, on an arm64 host such as a Mac. bb-box imports it from Docker on the host, or builds it there in a microVM of its own. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Docker in boxes
fields.description: Give each box its own Docker daemon, started by its first docker command, with its data on a disk of the box's own. Each box has its own kernel, so this needs no privilege on the host.

fields.label: Docker disk (GiB)
fields.description: The most each box's Docker disk may grow to. It takes only what Docker writes, and goes with the box.

fields.label: Root disk (GiB)
fields.description: The most a box's root disk may grow to when no disk size is asked for. It takes only what the box writes.

fields.label: Network profiles
fields.description: msb's network profiles for each box, comma-separated: public reaches the internet, private the host's local networks and tailnet, where BB's server often is.

fields.label: Most boxes
fields.description: The most bb-box microVMs on the host at once, running or stopped, counting those of every bb-box install that uses it.

fields.label: Memory kept free (MiB)
fields.description: A new box is refused if the host would have less memory than this left, after the memory of the running boxes.

fields.label: Memory overcommit
fields.description: How many times the host's memory the boxes may take in all, after the memory kept free: 1 to 4. At 1, each box counts at its full memory. Above 1, a new box also needs memory free on the host now. Raise it for mostly idle boxes.

drivers.label: Hetzner Cloud
drivers.description: Linux boxes on x86 or Arm, with or without a desktop, as containers on Docker hosts that bb-box makes in a Hetzner Cloud project as boxes need them, and deletes once they are idle.

fields.label: API token
fields.description: A Read & Write API token of the Hetzner Cloud project bb-box makes its hosts in, from the project's Security page. The project should hold nothing else.

fields.label: Location
fields.description: Where hosts are made, such as nbg1 (Nuremberg), fsn1 (Falkenstein) or hel1 (Helsinki): near BB's server, as a desktop's stream crosses between them.

fields.label: Server type
fields.description: The type of every host, such as cpx42 (8 cores, 16 GB, 320 GB disk). A box at its largest must fit one, with the memory kept free.

fields.label: Arm server type
fields.description: The type of the hosts for linux-arm64 boxes, an Ampere type such as cax31 (8 cores, 16 GB, 160 GB disk). Empty offers no arm64 boxes. Arm hosts have their own host image.

fields.label: Most hosts
fields.description: The most hosts at once. At this many, a box that fits on none of them is refused.

fields.label: Idle minutes
fields.description: A host with no box for this long is deleted. Hetzner bills by the started hour, so a shorter time saves little and makes acquires wait for a new host more often.

fields.label: Monthly limit (EUR)
fields.description: bb-box makes no host when this calendar month's spend so far, and an hour more of every host with the new one, would pass this many euros before VAT. A busy host keeps running until it is idle. 0 sets no limit. Hetzner has no limit of its own: set a cost alert in its Console too.

fields.label: Host image
fields.description: What hosts start from. An image name, such as ubuntu-26.04, is the base of the host image bb-box builds as a snapshot, with Docker, Tailscale and the box images in it, and rebuilds weekly or when its scripts change, keeping two; until the first is built, hosts start from the image itself. A snapshot's ID makes hosts start from that snapshot, and bb-box builds none.

fields.label: SSH from
fields.description: Only with the tailnet off: the addresses, as CIDRs separated by commas, that may reach a host's SSH over the internet, such as BB's server's public address. With the tailnet on, a host's SSH is reached on the tailnet alone.

fields.label: Linux image
fields.description: The image linux boxes run. setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Desktop image
fields.description: The image linux-desktop-cpu boxes, and linux-desktop boxes when GPU desktops are on, run. setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Wayland desktop image
fields.description: The image linux-desktop-wayland-cpu boxes run: Sway on Wayland, drawn by the CPU. setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off.

fields.label: Docker in boxes
fields.description: Give each box its own Docker daemon, started by its first docker command. Each runs as a privileged container, which can take over the Docker host. Off, or on rootless Docker, boxes say No Docker.

fields.label: Most boxes
fields.description: The most bb-box containers on the host at once, running or stopped, counting those of every bb-box install that uses it.

fields.label: Memory kept free (MiB)
fields.description: A new box is refused if the host would have less memory than this left, after the memory limits of the running boxes.

fields.label: Network
fields.description: The Docker network bb-box makes for its boxes, apart from the host's other containers.

drivers.label: Namespace
drivers.description: Macs and Linux machines rented by the minute from Namespace, one machine for each box, ended when the box is released or at the plan's longest life.

fields.label: API token
fields.description: A revocable token for the Namespace workspace, from nsc token create, granted the instance actions the guide lists. It is kept as a secret and never shown.

fields.label: API region
fields.description: us or eu: where bb-box calls Namespace's API and its SSH gateway. Where the machines run is the workspace's regional preference, which Namespace's support sets.

fields.label: macOS version
fields.description: The macOS a box runs, as Namespace's base images name it, such as 26.x.

fields.label: Most machines
fields.description: The most Namespace machines bb-box has at once. Each box is one machine, billed by the minute while it exists.

fields.label: Longest life (hours)
fields.description: How long the workspace's plan lets a machine live: 3 hours on Developer, 5 on Team, up to 24 on Business. A box ends then, and its thread hears an hour ahead.

fields.label: Largest machine
fields.description: The largest Mac bb-box asks for, as cores x memory in GB, such as 6x14. A box that needs a larger one is refused before bb-box asks Namespace, so another backend can take it. Empty: the largest the workspace allows, which bb-box reads from Namespace when the token may, or learns the first time Namespace refuses a Mac for its size.

fields.label: Shared iOS hosts
fields.description: Whether Namespace lends ios boxes as macOS users on a shared host: a Namespace Mac made for an ios box that finds no slot on a pool Mac or a Tart host, and deleted when its last box goes. It lends once bb-box has measured that Namespace's Macs run the iOS Simulator. A host takes the workspace's one Mac, so no macos box starts on Namespace while it lives.

fields.label: Slots a host lends at most
fields.description: Empty: bb-box estimates it from the Mac's cores, memory and video encoder, as for a pool Mac.

fields.label: Slots a host keeps ready
fields.description: Ready slots a host keeps while it holds a box.

fields.label: Slots a host resets at once
fields.description: Released slots a host sweeps at once, at most.

fields.label: Disk a host keeps free (GiB)
fields.description: Below this much free disk, a host makes no new slot.

kinds.label: Linux
kinds.description: A Linux box for builds, backend services and the agent's own work.

kinds.label: Linux desktop
kinds.description: A Linux desktop on a GPU, for computer use, browsers and app development.

kinds.label: Linux desktop
kinds.description: A Linux desktop drawn by the CPU, for computer use and browsers.

kinds.label: Linux desktop on Wayland
kinds.description: A Linux desktop on Wayland (Sway), drawn by the CPU, for computer use, browsers and apps built for Wayland. X11-only apps do not run there.

kinds.label: Windows desktop
kinds.description: A Windows desktop for computer use, browsers and Windows apps.

kinds.label: Android emulator
kinds.description: An Android emulator device, a phone, foldable or tablet, on a Linux VM: for installing, running and testing Android apps, shared with a person in the panel.

kinds.label: macOS
kinds.description: A Mac for builds and Apple's tools.

kinds.label: macOS desktop
kinds.description: A macOS desktop for computer use and app development.

kinds.label: iOS Simulator
kinds.description: An iOS Simulator device, an iPhone or iPad, on a macOS VM, or in a slot on a shared Mac or VM: for installing, running and testing iOS apps, shared with a person in the panel.

kinds.label: Linux on arm64
kinds.description: A Linux box on arm64. amd64 container images and x86_64 binaries do not run there.

kinds.label: Linux desktop on arm64
kinds.description: A Linux desktop on arm64, drawn by the CPU. amd64 container images and x86_64 binaries do not run there.

kinds.label: Windows desktop on arm64
kinds.description: A Windows desktop on arm64, for computer use, browsers and Windows apps. x64 apps run under Windows' emulation, more slowly; x64 drivers do not.
